title: Gateway: whitelist + validate quickstart template telemetry headers
author: Brian Murphy
release_notes: Gateway now accepts a small, validated set of quickstart template telemetry headers and propagates them internally for adoption metrics.
description:
Context: DevEx quickstart templates need a reliable, low-cardinality way to tag traffic as template-generated so we can measure activation funnel and time-to-first-success without relying on parsing user-agent strings. Today the API gateway drops unknown `x-*` headers by default; templates adding a telemetry header would silently lose that tag. This PR introduces an explicit allowlist in the gateway for a small set of template telemetry headers and performs strict validation to prevent abuse, high-cardinality explosions, and accidental PII leakage.

What this does: Adds a `template telemetry` header allowlist and validator at the gateway edge. Allowed headers are normalized into a structured internal context object that can be consumed by downstream logging/metrics/analytics (follow-up PRs). Invalid values are rejected with a 400 (clear error message) to avoid partial/ambiguous telemetry.

Allowed headers (v1): `x-redwood-template-id` (e.g. `rag-agent`), `x-redwood-template-version` (semver like `0.3.1`), `x-redwood-template-lang` (`python`|`typescript`), `x-redwood-template-origin` (`cli`|`github`), `x-redwood-template-otel` (`enabled`|`disabled`).

Validation rules: values must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` (lowercase enforced), max length 64, no whitespace, no commas/quotes/newlines. `x-redwood-template-version` is additionally checked as semver-like `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional `-prerelease` suffix. Any header not in the allowlist continues to be stripped by default.

Security/privacy notes: These headers are intended to be low-cardinality and non-user-content. This PR does not accept arbitrary key/value tagging. We do not log raw request headers; we only log the validated, normalized fields. Review requested from Security and Observability to confirm cardinality + redaction posture.

Operational notes: This is required for the Quickstart Templates KPI dashboard (PM-912). Follow-up work will plumb these fields into usage analytics (Console filter work) and template repos will keep sending these headers behind an opt-in flag to avoid issues with restrictive corporate proxies.

Testing: Added unit tests for allowlist behavior, validation failures, normalization, and a regression test that unknown headers are still dropped.
commits: gateway: add template telemetry header allowlist + parser
gateway: validate template telemetry values (regex + max len + semver)
gateway: add structured context fields for telemetry tags
tests: add allowlist/validation coverage + negative cases
docs(dev): add notes to gateway header policy README
conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry): Can we guarantee these won’t become high-cardinality? We’ve been burned by “just one tag” before.

Brian Murphy (author): Agree. Values are constrained to <=64 chars + strict charset and we force lowercase. Also only a fixed set of header names. No arbitrary tags. Added tests for rejection and documented examples. If we see unexpected cardinality we can also sample/drop downstream, but the intent is low-cardinality only.
Allison Grant (Observability): Please avoid propagating these as span attributes by default; attributes on every span can get expensive and hard to control.

Brian Murphy (author): Ack. This PR only stores them in request context. No tracing attributes are added here. Downstream plumbing (analytics) will be explicit and limited to request-level events only.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (Security): Returning 400 on invalid header values could be abused to create a minor DoS (clients retry) or cause confusing failures. Consider stripping invalid values instead of rejecting?

Brian Murphy (author): Good call. I leaned 400 to avoid silently losing telemetry + making debugging hard. But we can soften: only reject if a whitelisted header is present but invalid; otherwise ignore. That’s already the case. Also error message does not echo user-provided value; it only states which header is invalid and the allowed format.
Nikhil Sharma (PM, Hosted API): We need this for KPI attribution, but we also need to make sure it’s opt-in client-side due to proxy/header restrictions.

Brian Murphy (author): Yup. DevEx templates will gate sending these headers behind `REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1` (separate PR in quickstarts repo). Added a note to the PR description and gateway README.
CI Bot: gateway-unit-tests (pass), gateway-lint (pass), security-sast (pass), dependency-audit (pass).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Security): Approved after confirming (1) no raw header logging and (2) error messages don’t reflect header values.
Allison Grant (Observability): Approved with note: keep these fields off default span attributes; add any tracing usage behind a separate review.
Logan Wright (Telemetry): Approved. Please coordinate with Console/Analytics before emitting new dimensions into metrics.
